module_name: Platform Ecosystem: X, TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, Reddit, Bluesky/AT Protocol, Threads
module_description: Module 2 compares platforms as data environments: what is publicly retrievable, what the API exposes, how ranking (For You vs follow graph) shapes what data even means, and why platform choice determines feasible questions. It includes the 2025-2026 landscape where decentralized/federated networks (Bluesky/ActivityPub) became uniquely analyzable due to open firehose access, and where TikTok's data affordances dominate short-form video analysis.
core_concepts: Platform data affordances: what each API returns
Ranking logic (recommender feed vs chronological vs follow graph)
Openness spectrum from open firehose to gated research access
Decentralized and federated social media (ActivityPub, AT Protocol)
learning_outcomes: C4 Compare platforms on data availability, API openness and ranking logic
C3 Justify platform choice for a given research or business question
C5 Interpret why identical metrics mean different things across platforms
methods_models: Openness scoring based on API availability, rate limits and cost tiers
evaluation_metrics: Qualitative comparison graded with a rubric; metric reproduction exercise (compute a metric from raw data vs dashboard)
pitfalls_limitations: Comparing counts across platforms without normalizing audience size; assuming chronological data from an algorithmic feed; ignoring that metrics are defined per-platform
tools_stack: Bluesky Jetstream/public API, TikTokApi or TikTok Research API sandbox, Reddit API (praw), YouTube Data API, yt-dlp for public media
commercial_platforms: Read-only demos of TikTok Creative Center, X analytics, YouTube Studio analytics side by side
tools_access_cost: Platform API tiers and quotas; Meta Content Library is gated to academic institutions; some research environments started charging teams in 2026
lab_activities: For each of 3 platforms, collect 1,000 posts on the same topic, tabulate available fields, and write a 1-page comparability note
datasets_apis: Public topic corpora (e.g. disaster/topic hashtag on X and Bluesky) plus YouTube comment sample
assessment_methods: Written analysis/design document plus a short quiz; graded on correctness of concepts and quality of justification
data_collection_workflow: Define the question -> choose platform and access route -> collect via API or permitted scrape -> archive raw with checksums -> clean and document schema -> analyse -> preserve dataset and code
textbooks: Zafarani et al., Social Media Mining, ch. 2 (data sources)
Bruns, Are Filter Bubbles Real? (2019) for feed logic
key_papers: arXiv 2505.09877 - Studying Digital Platforms in Scant Data Access Times (2025)
Documentation of Bluesky AT Protocol firehose for research
trends_2024_2026: 2026 trend: platform divergence grew - open protocols (AT Protocol) vs closed enterprise access (Meta), with TikTok/Reels/Shorts as the default content surface for analytics on video
industry_relevance: Social media analyst, market-insights researcher, and data-journalist roles; this module is used for social listening, brand/issue monitoring, and audience research, and is referenced by industry certifications such as Meta Blueprint, Hootsuite Social Marketing, and Google Analytics.
localization_context: Taught with Indonesian-language material (IndoBERT/IndoRoBERTa/NusaBERT, InSet lexicon, Indonesian social datasets) so students can reproduce the analysis on local corpora; comparisons are made against Anglocentric benchmarks whose labels often transfer poorly.
ethics_regulation: Platform Terms of Service, UU PDP No. 27/2022 (Indonesian personal data protection), GDPR for EU-origin data, and IRB-style review for any data involving private individuals; public is not the same as consentable for social data.
case_study_scenarios: Which platform would you use to track an Indonesian election issue, and what can each platform actually tell you?
deliverable_format: Comparative platform memo plus small multi-platform dataset (CSV/JSON)
